data.title: Richard Parry Joins Board of Directors of Bimini Capital Management
data.description: In Vero Beach, Florida, on September 14, 2026, Bimini Capital Management, Inc. data.title: Quantum Appoints Mike Heuer as Chief Information Officer
data.description: Today, Quantum Corporation (Nasdaq: QMCO) based in Centennial, Colorado, has appointed Mike Heuer as its new Chief Information Officer. This announcement comes as Heuer steps into the role, where he will oversee Quantum's worldwide information technology division. He will be responsible for managing enterprise applications, data operations, AI implementation, IT infrastructure, and cybersecurity measures. Hugues Meyrath, the President and CEO of Quantum, expressed confidence in Heuer's capabilities, citing his track record of merging technology strategies with corporate goals and driving large-scale transformations within organizations.

data.title: Revolution Medicines Announces U.S. FDA Breakthrough Therapy Designation for RASONQUE™ (daraxonrasib) in Combination with Chemotherapy for First Line Metastatic Pancreatic Cancer
data.description: Revolution Medicines, Inc. headquartered in Redwood City, California, disclosed that the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has awarded Breakthrough Therapy Designation to RASONQUE (daraxonrasib), its RAS(ON) multi-selective inhibitor. The designation is specifically for the treatment of treatment-naïve metastatic pancreatic adenocarcinoma (PDAC) in conjunction with gemcitabine and nab-paclitaxel (GnP), a common chemotherapy regimen for PDAC patients. RASONQUE was recently approved by the FDA for adult patients with metastatic PDAC who have had at least one previous systemic therapy or are not suitable for multiagent systemic therapy. The company, publicly traded on Nasdaq under RVMD, is dedicated to developing innovative medicines for patients with RAS-addicted cancers.

data.title: Agomab Announces Positive Phase 1 Results for AGMB-447 in Patients with Idiopathic Pulmonary Fibrosis and Design of Phase 2 INSPIRIA Study
data.description: Today, Agomab Therapeutics revealed encouraging findings from a Phase 1 trial of AGMB-447 conducted in patients suffering from idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF). The study showed promising results in terms of effectiveness and safety of the drug. This signifies a significant advancement in the treatment of IPF, a serious and often fatal lung disease. The results indicate that AGMB-447 could offer a new and more effective therapeutic option for IPF patients. This is a key development in the medical field, as there has been a long-standing need for improved treatment options for this debilitating condition that affects approximately 100,000 individuals in the United States alone. The positive outcome of the Phase 1 trial paves the way for further research and development of AGMB-447 as a potential treatment for IPF.
